messages.subject: RNAseq Pathway Analysis w/ Bioconductor package 'pathview'
parts:
I have very little experience with R and I'm trying to use the Bioconductor package 'pathview' to make some KEGG pathways for RNAseq data.  I read the vignette, but am still not sure what data to import and how the data needs to be set-up.  Does anyone have any experience with 'pathview'?  I'll be at the mtg on Tues 6/23.  

Thanks,
Dorothy

messages.author: 05bda608df45c6f4
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: RNAseq Pathway Analysis w/ Bioconductor package 'pathview'
parts:
Hi Dorothy,

I'm not familiar with the package, but after reading through some of the documentation, it seems that at the most basic level you want a column of data representing relative gene expression for many different genes between treatment conditions. In the example they give, it's microarray data, and "pair-wise gene expression changes between DCIS (disease) and HN (control) samples." If you're working with RNA-seq data, however, I'm guessing you'd want to use some of sort of metric like ratio of Fragments Per Kilobase of transcript per Million mapped reads (FPKM) between two samples.

Hopefully that gets you at least part of the way to your data import/set up.

From there, the call to pathview() also seems to require the study species in question and the pathway of interest. I'm not sure what species you're working with, but I'm assuming it's important that you're working with a well-characterized pathway and using gene names that Pathview recognizes in order to get good results.

Hope that helps,
Evan
